messages.content: Help me parse the HTTP response body from an entity `httpResponseEntity` using a specific parser function `responseParser` that handles the content, with a parser configuration `defaultParserConfig` in an Elasticsearch multi-cluster search test?

function.name: CCSDuelIT_parseEntity
function.description: Parses an HttpEntity using the provided entity parser function and parser configuration, and returns the parsed response of type Resp. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

entity.description: The HttpEntity to parse. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

entityParser.description: The function that will parse the XContentParser into the desired response type. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

parserConfig.description: The configuration for the XContentParser. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

- entity: string representation of the HttpEntity. In the context of the test, we might have a variable `httpResponseEntity`. We need to pass it as a string representation. Usually, we might pass the variable name or the actual string. The tool expects a string representation of the Java object. So we can pass `"httpResponseEntity"`.

- entityParser: string representation of the function that will parse the XContentParser into the desired response type. That is `responseParser`. So we pass `"responseParser"`.

- parserConfig: string representation of the parser configuration. That is `defaultParserConfig`. So we pass `"defaultParserConfig"`.

Thus we call the function with those arguments.

We need to produce a JSON object with the function call. The tool expects a JSON object with the function name and arguments. The function name is `functions.CCSDuelIT_parseEntity`. The arguments are an object with keys `entity`, `entityParser`, `parserConfig`.

Thus we produce:

{
  "name": "functions.CCSDuelIT_parseEntity",
  "arguments": {
    "entity": "httpResponseEntity",
    "entityParser": "responseParser",
    "parserConfig": "defaultParserConfig"
  }
}

We should not include any other keys. The tool will parse this and return the parsed response.
